transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (CTO, Silvercrest), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Marcus Li (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on cost model and unit economics for Silvercrest's planned assistant product. Covered success criteria, workload sizing, recommended benchmarks, batching/caching knobs, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Action items and benchmark plan agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um, goal is to scope the POC and make sure we all align on success criteria and cost expectations.
[00:12] Daniel Reyes: Yep, thanks Maya. Quick context: we're building an internal assistant for our enterprise customers, needs to hit sub-500ms tail latency for interactive flows, and also support async long-form summarization for batch jobs. Budget for POC is roughly $6k month but we can flex if numbers make sense.
[00:30] Liam Chen: Got it. Can you say more about expected QPS and token mix? That'll drive per-token estimates and batching strategy.
[00:40] Priya Nair: For interactive: peak 80 QPS, avg around 25. Typical prompt + response token mix is 50 input / 120 output tokens for short assist; long-form summarization is up to 10k input tokens but run as nightly batch ~10 jobs.
[01:00] Marcus Li: And infra constraints: we prefer VPC/private deployment but for POC open to hosted if we can validate perf and security. We'll need SOC2 docs and KMS support.
[01:12] Maya Patel: Cool. From Redwood side we'll propose two modes: hosted fast path to validate latency and model quality, then Dedicated or Private for production. For cost modeling we should break down per-token cost with knobs for batching, KV/prefix caching, and model variant selection.
[01:30] Liam Chen: Right. Quick back-of-envelope: for a gpt-like 13B open model we typically see X tokens/sec per GPU depending on quantization. For interactive use at 80 QPS with 170 tokens per request, you hit roughly 13.6k tokens/s sustained — that's about N GPUs unless you leverage aggressive batching and short-circuit caching. (note: transcription error: 'N GPUs' was 'three GPUs')
[01:58] Priya Nair: Sorry you said three GPUs?
[02:00] Liam Chen: Yeah, for that workload with conservative batching maybe 2-3 dedicated GPUs; but with prefix caching on repeated prompts we can reduce tokens generated per request by ~25-40% for assistant flows.
[02:18] Daniel Reyes: Important for us: tail latency at p95/p99. We can't sacrifice the p99. What's typical for Redwood hosted vs dedicated?
[02:27] Maya Patel: Hosted we have faster onboarding and can run a benchmark in days; typical p95 for hosted on small models with streaming is 200-350ms, p99 can vary but we hit targets with dedicated capacity and latency SLOs. Private/VPC adds some network overhead but stays within SLO when sized properly.
[02:45] Marcus Li: On cost, can you show per-token examples? We need to compare to our internal costs and vertex pricing.
[02:52] Liam Chen: Sure, sample per-token math we walked through: model compute cost per token varies by model/quantization. For an optimized 13B quantized profile we estimate $0.00005 per token at high utilization as an equivalent hosted blended rate — that's illustrative. If you increase batching and reach >70% GPU utilization, unit cost drops ~20-30%.
[03:15] Priya Nair: That $0.00005 — does that include prefix cache savings?
[03:20] Liam Chen: No, that's raw generation. With prefix/KV caching and request-level caching you'll effectively pay for fewer generated tokens; so effective cost per logical response can drop to $0.000035-0.00004 depending on cache hit rates.
[03:34] Daniel Reyes: And what about the long-form summarization jobs? Those big 10k token jobs — how do you recommend batching/queueing?
[03:42] Liam Chen: For long jobs we usually route to a batch queue on dedicated GPUs optimized for long sequences — different kernel choices and memory management. You can schedule nightly runs to avoid peak interactive load. Cost per token can be slightly higher due to longer context but you get throughput gains via larger micro-batches. We'll measure with a 1-hour throughput benchmark.
[04:03] Maya Patel: For the POC success criteria let's agree on a few measurable items: 1) p95 interactive latency < 500ms and p99 < 1.2s on hosted benchmark; 2) cost per active session below $0.10/session assuming X prompts/day; 3) end-to-end quality parity with your current model (Priya will define sample evaluation prompts).
[04:24] Priya Nair: We'll provide a 5k prompt set with relevance/QA and a separate 200 long-form docs for summarization.
[04:31] Daniel Reyes: Timeline wise we want to validate within 4 weeks: week 1 onboarding and data prep, week 2 hosted benchmark runs, week 3 iteration on model variant and batching, week 4 final report + cost model.
[04:46] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. We'll push a benchmark spec and schedule the run early next week.
[04:51] Marcus Li: Security — we need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, and audit logs. Can you share network diagrams and compliance detail?
[04:59] Maya Patel: Yes — I'll include the security appendix and SOC2 certs in the follow up. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated; hosted can integrate with cloud KMS for enterprise customers.
[05:12] Liam Chen: On benchmarking specifics: we'll run three tests: 1) interactive latency test at 80 QPS for 10 minutes ramping to steady state, collect p50/p95/p99; 2) throughput test with 500 concurrent pipes to estimate GPU tokens/sec; 3) nightly batch test running 200 long-form docs to validate total runtime and cost. We'll capture raw logs and cost breakdown per token.
[05:40] Daniel Reyes: Good. For the cost model spreadsheet please include assumptions: GPU type, quantization profile (8-bit vs 4-bit), cache hit rate sensitivity (0, 25, 50%), and batching sizes. We want sensitivity analysis so we can pick ops knobs.
[05:55] Maya Patel: We'll include those rows. Also we'll add a column for routing policy e.g., fall back to cheaper model for non-critical paths — that often reduces cost by 15-25%.
[06:05] Priya Nair: Any limitations in hosted for telemetry? We need token-level traces for debugging.
[06:10] Liam Chen: Hosted includes token-level cost and latency traces per request in the Console; we'll make sure your team has access for the POC. For Private/Dedicated you get full logs in your VPC.
[06:22] Daniel Reyes: Ok one last question on SLA and regression: if a model update regresses quality, do you have eval hooks and automatic rollback?
[06:30] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run regression checks against your eval sets and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model versions. We'll demo that if POC moves to Dedicated.
[06:40] Daniel Reyes: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[06:43] Maya Patel: Recap: Maya sends cost model spreadsheet, SOC2 and security docs. Liam runs benchmark spec and sets up hosted test; Daniel/ Priya provide the 5k prompt set and long-form docs. We'll aim to start the benchmark next Tuesday and have mid-point review in week 2.
[06:58] Priya Nair: I'll send the datasets and expected evaluation metrics by Sunday.
[07:03] Marcus Li: I'll coordinate network access and IP allowlist for the hosted bench.
[07:08] Maya Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up over email with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.
[07:12] Daniel Reyes: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes/Artifacts referenced:
- Benchmark spec (will be shared): 80 QPS interactive, 5k prompt set, 200 long-form docs for summarization
- Cost model spreadsheet (attached after call)
- SOC2 + Security appendix (attached)
- Sample routing policy doc

Action items (in call):
- Maya Patel: Send cost model spreadsheet and SOC2/security appendix by 2026-12-11
- Liam Chen: Define benchmark spec and run 1-hour latency/throughput tests; share logs by 2026-12-16
- Daniel Reyes / Priya Nair: Provide 5k prompt set and 200 long-form documents by 2026-12-13
